history: I have always been curious about how things work. How was a game built? What ideas shaped it? Why was a piece of software designed one way rather than another?
Those questions are what draw me to development. I enjoy looking beyond what is on the screen to understand the decisions and the code behind it.
What I love most is that learning never really ends: the more I understand, the more I discover there is still to explore.

epitech.description: Studying computer science, building a foundation in C and C++, and developing web applications with React and TypeScript.

epi-studio.description: Developing my web development skills within an open-source association, working with Java, Spring Boot, Vue.js, and TypeScript.

spinetime.description: A web development internship focused on KinéDuQuotidien, an application for physiotherapists, using React and TypeScript.

saesth: Saesth is a desktop application for creating a workspace that feels right for you, combining natural ambient sounds with customizable keyboard sounds.
Build your own sound packs and switch between them to suit your mood, whether you are working, studying, or simply enjoying a quieter moment.
Built with Rust, Tauri, and React, the project brings sound customization into a single desktop experience.
slot-addict: A horror game in which you play as someone consumed by a slot machine addiction, trapped in a dream shaped by that obsession.
Search for coins, pull the lever, and keep playing while something nearby turns the familiar ritual into a threat.
Built in Godot with GDScript, the game explores the tension between the urge to play and the part of you that wants to stop.
patcher: Patcher is a desktop application for Windows and Linux that helps you write and organize release notes in Markdown.
Create different types of release notes for your projects, with a focus on preparing updates for GitHub releases.
Built with Java, Gradle, JDBC, and SQLite, it provides a dedicated workspace for documenting what changes between versions.
